html:
SMTO-WEB-0033 — SMTO only saw part of a page, so it can't say "that's all"

GUID: 034e0ffe-9695-5821-9057-70f6706b01e6
Slug: research-exhaustive-claim-from-truncated-source
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The answer says something like "these are all of them" or "none exist", but SMTO only read part of a page. Seeing part of a page can't prove nothing else is there.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to limit its statement to what it actually saw. The page was cut off, so claims like "all" or "none" can't be proven from it.
  2. If you need a complete list, ask SMTO to read the remaining pages of that source, for example the next page of results. Seeing the whole source is the only way to support an "all" or "none" statement.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. The answer is then shown even though its "all" or "none" statement wasn't fully checked.

What success looks like

  • The answer says "in the results SMTO saw" or similar, or is backed by the complete source.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rely on an "all" or "none" statement unless SMTO saw the whole source.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected a claim whose fact values use exhaustive wording (all listings, only model/product, no other, none exist, exhaustive) while at least one supporting source is marked truncated.

What this means

  • A claim uses exhaustive wording while at least one supporting source is marked truncated. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • A claim uses exhaustive wording while at least one supporting source is marked truncated.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect source truncation flags and phrases asserting completeness.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_exhaustive_claim_from_truncated_source in _validate_answer. Narrow the claim to the observed portion, or acquire complete (non-truncated) evidence, for example additional pages or a narrower query, before making an exhaustive statement.
  • Narrow the claim to the observed results or acquire sufficient complete evidence through an authorized route.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The answer limits its claim to the observed portion unless complete evidence supports exhaustiveness.

What not to do

  • Do not claim every item was checked when the underlying observation was truncated.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
